text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 25 in history.
1533 - King Henry VIII of England, defying Rome, married his second wife Anne Boleyn.
1540 - St Edmund Campion, English scholar and Jesuit martyr, born. He was hanged for treason in 1581 and canonized in 1970.
1627 - Robert Boyle, Irish chemist and physicist, born. Boyle's Law states that the pressure and volume of gas are inversely proportional.

1759 - Robert Burns, Scottish poet, born. Noted for using Scottish dialect in his poems, such as "Tam o'Shanter", Burns became national poet of Scotland and Burn's Night is celebrated each year on this day.
1874 - William Somerset Maugham, English novelist and playwright, born. Noted for the books "Of Human Bondage" and "The Moon and Sixpence.
1878 - A Turkish steamer became the first ship to be sunk by a torpedo, fired from a Russian boat.
1882 - Adeline Virginia Woolf, author and critic, born. A member of the Bloomsbury Group, her books include "To the Lighthouse" and "The Waves".
1866 - Wilhelm Furtwangler, German conductor and composer, born. Best known for his interpretations of Beethoven and Wagner.
1899 - Paul-Henri Spaak, Belgian statesman, born. In 1938 he became Belgium's first socialist premier.
1919 - The League of Nations, forerunner of the U.N., was founded.
1924 - The first Winter Olympics began at Chaminox, France.
1928 - Eduard Shevardnadze, Georgian head of state, born. He was Soviet foreign minister from 1985 until his resignation in 1990, and took over in Georgia after Zviad Gamsakhurdia had been ousted.
1935 - Antonio Ramalho Eanes, Portuguese president 1976-86, born.
1947 - Al Capone, best known U.S. gangster who dominated the Chicago area, died. Indicted for tax evasion and imprisoned, Capone was released in 1939.
1950 - U.S. State Department official Alger Hiss was found guilty of perjury after he concealed his membership of the Communist Party.
1969 - The latest phase of Vietnam peace talks opened in Paris, the Allies pushing for the restoration of the de-militarised zone and the Communists for total withdrawal of American troops.
1971 - Army officers led by Idi Amin deposed Milton Obote and he became president of Uganda.
1971 - Charles Manson was found guilty of masterminding the killings of actress Sharon Tate and six others.
1975 - Sheikh Mujibur Rahman became president of Bangladesh and established a one-party state.
1980 - Abolhassan Bani-Sadr won Iran's first presidential election with 70 percent of the vote.
1983 - China commuted the death sentence, imposed on this day in 1981, on Mao Zedong's widow Jiang Qing.
1990 - Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto gave birth to a girl, the first-ever head of government to give birth while still in office.
1994 - Michael Jackson reached a multi-million dollar settlement with a boy who had accused him of sexual molestation.
1995 - A missile fired by Norway as part of a scientific research programme triggered an air defence alert in Russia.
1996 - The Council of Europe parliamentary assembly voted to admit Russia to the 38-nation body despite fierce criticism of its military crackdown in Chechnya and its human rights record.
